A Wonderful Stay in the Heart of Naples – with a Rooftop View You Won’t Forget!

We recently had the pleasure of staying at Napolinn B&B both before and after our Mediterranean cruise—on June 27 and again on July 5—and we could not have been more delighted with our experience.

From the moment we arrived, Guiliana, our host, made us feel genuinely welcome. As a couple traveling together, we really appreciated her warmth, personal attention, and helpful recommendations. She gave us fantastic local tips on where to eat and shop, which helped us make the most of our short time in Naples.

The location of Napolinn is absolutely ideal—right in the heart of the city, within easy walking distance of Naples’ top attractions, bustling shopping areas, and great restaurants. Whether you’re catching a cruise (like we were) or just exploring the city, you won’t find a more convenient base.

Our room was spacious, air-conditioned, and had a very comfortable bed, which was perfect after long travel days. We slept well both nights we stayed.

One of the standout features of Napolinn is the rooftop patio—it’s where breakfast is served, and it offers spectacular views of Naples. It’s the perfect place to start your day with a delicious cappuccino, latte, or espresso, alongside fresh croissants and cornetti. Sitting up there in the morning sun, looking out over the rooftops of Naples, was one of our favorite memories of the trip. Be sure to bring your camera—this spot is a hidden gem for photos!

A few additional notes for fellow travelers:

Elevator access is available, which is a big plus when arriving with luggage.

The rooms are quiet, despite the central location—great for a good night’s sleep.

Communication with the B&B (especially Guiliana) was easy and clear before and during our stay.

Check-in and check-out were smooth and efficient.

We would absolutely stay at Napolinn again and wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone visiting Naples. Thank you again, Guiliana.

This was my first time encountering bed bugs at a hostel. I stayed here from August 24th to 26th.

1. On the first night, I noticed a strange odor coming from the bed every now and then before falling asleep. Since I’m not one to make a fuss, I tried to ignore it. The next morning, the girl staying in the bunk above me mentioned that she had been bitten by bugs and needed to change beds. At the time, I didn’t think much of it since the bites on my body hadn’t become visible yet. Actually, that afternoon, I went back for a nap and woke up with bite marks. I thought they were mosquito bites, but looking back, they were classic bed bug bites: large, flat, red welts with a small dot in the center.
2. On the second day, I woke up with several obvious bites on my arms and legs. Since I’m usually prone to mosquito bites, I assumed I’d been bitten while out exploring (I really should have checked my body more carefully—I regret it now). The girl from the upper bunk had already moved out and asked if I’d been bitten too. I said no at the time, since accusing a place of having bed bugs is a serious matter.
3. By the third day, the bites on my exposed skin had significantly increased. As my trip was coming to an end, I went shopping and tried on some clothes. It was in the fitting room that I finally took a close look at my entire body—and I was horrified. I had very typical bed bug bites all over my back, shoulders, buttocks, and lower back. There were shocking clusters of bright red welts, with two or three large bites grouped together, inflamed and swollen. I had over thirty bites in total—it was terrifying. I immediately lost all interest in continuing my trip and went back to confront the hostel staff.

The staff’s reaction was quite interesting: they repeatedly insisted that "it could be anything." From start to finish, there was not a single word of comfort—just a cold suggestion to "relax" (as if I were making a big deal out of nothing).

I understand that if someone do a late check out, the host will charge the person but I have never been charged for a late check in. They could have had a better customer service and accommodate us. Modern, comfortable, and clean room in country setting 2+ km from Venice airport. Breakfast was excellent. Hosts are very welcoming and provide all info you need about local area and transfers to/from airport and Venice City Center.

The hotel is spotlessly clean and in a very quiet building. Breakfast was delicious, especially the pastry. It's just a short walk to the Metro and train stations, and very walkable to attractions like the Spanish Steps or Colosseum.
Not a complaint, just a suggestion: as someone who has chronic neck trouble, I always appreciate newer pillows when I can't travel with my own!

If you're looking for peace and quiet off the beaten path, this is it. Quite the opposite of Cortina D'Ampezzo, very quiet, not to say isolated, and frequented mostly by Italian tourists, it comes at the cost of lower elevation mountains and less spectacular scenery. The nearest towns of Cavalese and Tesero are quaint and have several good restaurants and at least one supermarket. The drive to Bolzano seems short, at 20-some kilometers, but it will take you 45 minutes on narrow, windy mountain roads. The restaurant has an excellent breakfast, quite lavish, and very friendly and helpful staff - we loved the staff here. The indoor/outdoor pool is very nice for kids and there are good hiking opportunities nearby. I would be tempted to return here at a lower room price. Note: this is a summer review.
The hotel is located right on a secondary road that may see some traffic in the tourist season, but soundproofing is good. A car (or strong legs and a bike) is almost mandatory in this area, even to get to the nearest town. 300 Euro a night seems rather pricey for what it offers, even in August, but the hotel is nevertheless full. Apartments are cleaned once a week, and an extra charge is required for daily cleaning, which seems unusual for a 4-star hotel.
We really enjoyed our stay here!
The host was very helpful and communicated very well. The location of the property is stunning and was a great hub for visiting the Aosta valley.

The building and room were beautiful and very clean. The staff were very polite and helpful. There was water, tea and cookies for guests in the room. Overall, it was a great stay and great value for money.
The room was cold, but better with the window open.

We had the most wonderful experience staying at this charming B&B, just a 10-minute walk from the castle — a perfect location for exploring the area without needing a car. The setting is both peaceful and picturesque, with a balcony view while enjoying your morning coffee that’s hard to beat: lush gardens and a glimpse of the castle in the distance. It’s a scene that feels like it’s been plucked from a storybook.
The breakfast each morning was a real highlight — fresh, generous, and absolutely delicious. You can taste the quality and care in every bite, much of it sourced directly from the garden just outside. The rooms and bathrooms were immaculately clean, beautifully decorated, and clearly designed with thought and intention. From high-quality mattresses to well-placed charging stations in every room, everything you could need for a comfortable stay has been anticipated.
The B&B is Davide’s childhood home, and that warmth is felt in every corner. The philosophy here is simple but powerful: treat every guest like they’re loved and part of the family — but never at the expense of professionalism. Catrin, Davide and the Conte family truly go above and beyond. From sharing local tips to recommending the most fantastic restaurants and spa experiences, their guidance added so much to our trip.
This wasn’t just a stay — it was an experience of genuine hospitality, connection, and care. We’ll absolutely be back.
Clean with amazing facilities. Super close walk to Lungomare/centre. Fitness centre was AMAZING and so waa the breakfast, amazing selection. Tons of parking available.

comfy bed, nice room well furnished, good breakfast,

Great location. Comfortable beds.

The host was very kind and welcoming, and the apartment itself was very clean, which we really appreciated. However, there were several downsides to the stay that future guests should be aware of.
The Wi-Fi connection is extremely limited—it only worked reliably in the stairwell or the bathroom. The location is quite remote, far from everything, and  unfortunately, there's no view at all despite being in a hillside area.

There is ongoing construction nearby, and while we didn’t have any direct issues, the neighbors didn’t seem very friendly—we often felt uncomfortable coming in or out of the property due to the stares.

Also worth noting: there is no parking space included, and you’ll need to pay €4 per night to park in a nearby area.

Overall, if you're looking for a very quiet and isolated stay and don’t need strong internet.. this may suit your needs. But for us, the lack of connectivity and difficult location made it a challenging stay, despite how lovely the host was.

Due to a delayed flight, we arrived outside of the requested check-in period (3-8pm), but we kept in touch with the staff via Booking.com, and they were very gracious and stayed until we arrived (almost 9:45pm). The hotel is on the second floor of a gorgeous old building right in the heart of Florence, and is a close walk to everything. Our room was very quiet and clean (with a beautiful fresco on the ceiling), and the air-conditioner worked well enough that we didn't suffer during the heat wave. 

The staff was also happy to order us a regular taxi to get to the airport (which arrived in 5 minutes). We asked them how much we should expect to pay, and the taxi bill was within a few euros of their estimated amount (€34, which was much better value than a private driver!)

A tip for those who are coming from the airport; when we arrived, there wasn't a single taxi at the airport, and it was impossible to call one via Uber (it would not connect us to a driver). There was also a lineup of about 100 people waiting for a taxi. It would have taken us all night! Either pre-arrange for a taxi to pick you up, OR, you can also take the tram. Just follow the instructions provided by the hotel on this site. It was very easy, and I think it cost us €3.50 for two people.
The room (and bathroom) was a bit small, but that is to be expected in Florence.

Extra blankets were stained yellow as if they were 100 years old and not sure if they were actually clean or not. Also, I believe check in is anytime after 2pm, but they only have someone there to give you the key until 4pm. Luckily, we arrived before 4pm, but if we did not, we were told that we would need to send photos of our passports and credit card over email in order to check in. This is not a safe procedure, booking.com has a banner explicitly telling clients to NOT send information such as identification and credit card information via email. I would not stay here again unfortunately.
